25-## Stability
26-
27:New releases come out many times a day, but the install command below gives you the **stable channel**: a release reaches it only after the full test suite and a two-hour, 600,000-page load test pass on that exact release, and only when an important fix is waiting or stable is a week old. Updates are never installed without your say-so unless you turn on automatic upgrades. After an upgrade, gbrain shows a one-time notice listing what changed in behaviour. Stable also comes with a written promise about which commands, flags, tools, config keys and output fields stay the same, and how much warning you get before one changes. [docs/STABILITY.md](docs/STABILITY.md) explains that promise, how often stable moves, how to pin a version or go back, and what the faster alpha channel is for.

--
36-> gbrainio terminal connect      # in a new terminal
37-> gbrainio workspace new         # pick a plan in the browser
38:> curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash   # skip if Bun 1.4.4+ is installed
39-> export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
40:> bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable   # the gbrain CLI only; no local brain
41-> # Claude Code (an existing gbrain entry is kept):
42-> (claude mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || claude mcp add --transport http --scope user gbrain https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup claude-code --instructions-only

It writes the [brain-first block](docs/guides/setup.md#brain-first-instructions) into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or Codex's `AGENTS.md` (a non-empty `AGENTS.override.md` instead when Codex has one) with a per-turn rule hook, and leaves the MCP entry alone; the same command with `--no-instructions` added takes them out.

119-### Connect GBrain to your AI client (MCP)
120-
121-- **Local stdio client:** `gbrain setup claude-code` or `gbrain setup codex` registers `gbrain serve` (lists the memory verbs; `--surface full` lists every tool) behind gbrain's launcher, so a session opened in a cloned repository never loads that repository's `bunfig.toml` or `.env`, and adds the brain-first instructions: agents seldom call a brain nobody told them about. Cursor, Windsurf and other stdio clients take `"$(command -v gbrain)" serve --surface starter --advertise verbs`.
122:- **Plugins with curated skills:** Codex `codex plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain@codex-plugin` + `codex plugin add gbrain@gbrain`; Claude Code `/plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain` + `/plugin install gbrain@gbrain`.
123-- **This brain from anywhere:** `gbrain mcp expose` publishes it on your Tailscale tailnet as a user service (`--funnel` for cloud agents such as Grok Bot, Muse and ChatGPT). [Guide](docs/guides/remote-mcp.md).
124:- **A brain on another host:** `gbrain connect https://your-host/mcp --token gbrain_xxx --install` (add `--agent codex` for Codex). Hosted brains use [native OAuth or a private handoff](docs/guides/hosted-harness-access.md); dashboard, clients and permissions live in [MCP administration](docs/mcp/ADMIN.md).

content.text:
I installed gbrain v0.60.734.0, and `gbrain --version` reports `gbrain 0.60.734.0`.

- **Bun:** the docs require Bun 1.4.4 or newer, so I installed Bun 1.4.4 with the official script. It's in `~/.bun/bin`.
- **gbrain:** I ran the README's install command with the version tag in place of `#stable`: `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0`. That resolved to commit `a278ddf`.
- **PATH:** your shell profile doesn't add `~/.bun/bin` to PATH yet, so run `export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"` in a new shell before using `gbrain`.

`gbrain doctor` stops with `no_brain`, which just means no brain has been created yet. I left two setup steps from the docs undone because they change your configuration, so you can choose when to run them:

```bash
gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding   # create a local brain
gbrain setup claude-code              # register the MCP server and add brain-first instructions to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
```

gbrain also printed a notice that this install now follows the stable channel. The docs say updates are only installed if you approve them or turn on automatic upgrades, so you'll stay on v0.60.734.0 unless you do one of those.
